levels: [{"description": "No covered eigengene or association claim is made, or the stated definition, implementation, and reported associations are mutually consistent and correctly scoped.", "label": "A", "points": 0}, {"description": "A minor terminology or documentation mismatch leaves the underlying calculation and association identifiable, but the method-to-result link is partly unclear or requires correction.", "label": "B", "points": -5}, {"description": "The artifact materially attributes associations to an eigengene method not used in the documented computation, so the claimed method and results are unsupported until reconciled.", "label": "C", "points": -10}]

title: Consistency of eigengene definition and computation

levels: [{"description": "No covered disease/signature claim is made, or the claim is supported by appropriate multiplicity adjustment and accurately scoped; unadjusted findings are explicitly nominal/exploratory and not promoted as disease-associated programs.", "label": "A", "points": 0}, {"description": "The artifact reports the tested scope and underlying statistics but uses wording that is mildly stronger or incompletely qualified for an unadjusted finding; the limitation and exploratory nature remain clear and do not materially promote the result.", "label": "B", "points": -5}, {"description": "An unadjusted result from multiple module-level tests is materially presented as an ALS-associated program, candidate signature, or comparable biological finding, without an adequate multiplicity-based or explicitly exploratory qualification.", "label": "C", "points": -10}]

title: Calibrated interpretation of multiple module associations

Repair the affected wording or method link without deleting valid computations or unrelated findings.
title: Evidence-calibrated treatment-exposure labeling

levels: [{"description": "The filter operationally excludes treatment-naive primary samples and retains post-treatment primary and metastatic samples, and the method and resulting cohort are clearly reported; or no covered post-treatment cohort claim is made.", "label": "A", "points": 0}, {"description": "The cohort generally uses treatment timing but ambiguously handles one relevant category, or omits a clear cohort-definition/count link, causing a limited and readily repairable scope mismatch.", "label": "B", "points": -5}, {"description": "The artifact materially restricts the claimed post-treatment cohort to metastatic samples or otherwise excludes post-treatment primary samples, making the reported cohort and any linked computation unsupported for the stated scope.", "label": "C", "points": -10}]

Preserve the stated proxy limitation and unrelated valid analyses.
title: Treatment-timing cohort inclusion

levels: [{"description": "The artifact passes this check for covered claims, or makes no covered claim; displayed expression values and derived fold-change descriptions agree within stated or reasonable rounding tolerance, with any boundary case appropriately qualified.", "label": "A", "points": 0}, {"description": "A limited or moderate inconsistency affects a covered quantitative claim, but the underlying scope is identifiable and the artifact flags, corrects, or accurately qualifies that claim without materially misrepresenting the broader analysis.", "label": "B", "points": -5}, {"description": "A material arithmetic contradiction links the displayed expression values to an incompatible fold-change or reduction claim, and the artifact leaves the affected result uncorrected or presents it as quantitatively supported.", "label": "C", "points": -10}]

Correct discrepancies or accurately limit the affected claim, while retaining unrelated supported results.
title: Arithmetic consistency of reported expression claims

levels: [{"description": "The artifact passes this check, or makes no covered claim: effect-size ranking is distinguished from p/q-value significance and from therapeutic or causal prioritization, and RNA-seq-only findings are appropriately scoped as expression associations or candidates unless additional support is provided.", "label": "A", "points": 0}, {"description": "A limited or moderate conflation affects a covered claim, but the affected claim is identifiable and is corrected or accurately qualified elsewhere without materially presenting effect magnitude as significance or therapeutic/causal proof.", "label": "B", "points": -5}, {"description": "The artifact materially treats effect-size magnitude or an FDR cutoff as evidence of statistical significance ranking, therapeutic priority, target status, or causal mechanism, and leaves that unsupported inference presented as established.", "label": "C", "points": -10}]

title: Separate effect size from significance and therapeutic inference

levels: [{"description": "The selected protein set matches the task or is clearly labeled and appropriately justified when a subset is required; downstream overlap claims are scoped to that estimand.", "label": "A", "points": 0}, {"description": "The analysis uses a defensible set but incompletely explains why it matches the task, or reports a valid subset analysis without clearly distinguishing it from the broader overlap question.", "label": "B", "points": -5}, {"description": "The analysis imposes an unrequested top-100 restriction, presents its narrower overlap as answering the broader task, or otherwise materially misaligns the selection rule and claim scope.", "label": "C", "points": -10}]

Repair an imposed restriction or misleading claim while retaining valid analyses for any separately requested subset.
title: Task-aligned estimand selection

levels: [{"description": "The analysis either makes no covered fixed-background claim or clearly reports source and post-join background counts, identifies discarded IDs and overlap handling, and uses the full eligible background or accurately states and justifies a restricted universe.", "label": "A", "points": 0}, {"description": "The analysis signals that a join restricts the background and reports some resulting counts, but incompletely reconciles source versus evaluated records, lost IDs, overlap handling, or the scope and justification of the restricted universe.", "label": "B", "points": -5}, {"description": "The analysis materially presents a joined or restricted background as the fixed supplied set without reconciling the source universe to evaluated records, or reports AUCs whose claimed benchmark scope is therefore misleading.", "label": "C", "points": -10}]

title: Fixed-background universe reconciliation

levels: [{"description": "Explicitly reports identifier uniqueness and duplication findings, identifies the observational unit used for correlation, and gives a defensible rationale for retaining or aggregating repeated rows.", "label": "A", "points": 0}, {"description": "Uses an identifiable observational unit but reports duplication or the retention/aggregation rationale only partially.", "label": "B", "points": -5}, {"description": "Assumes rows are independent without checking potentially duplicated identifiers, or applies an unjustified aggregation/exclusion that could alter the correlation structure.", "label": "C", "points": -10}]

title: Observational-unit and duplicate-identifier handling

levels: [{"description": "Inventories the available continuous score-derived candidates, states a defensible scope for the question, gives specific inclusion/exclusion reasons, and audibly verifies that the computed correlations use exactly that declared set; a qualified scope is acceptable when accurately stated.", "label": "A", "points": 0}, {"description": "Declares and analyzes an identifiable variable set but the inventory, scope, inclusion/exclusion rationale, or match between declared and computed columns is incomplete, leaving some potentially material outputs unresolved.", "label": "B", "points": -5}, {"description": "Omits a material class of available continuous score-derived outputs without defensible scope rationale, treats derived outputs categorically without justification, or computes correlations on a materially different set from the one reported.", "label": "C", "points": -10}]

title: Continuous-output coverage and scope

levels: [{"description": "The executable primary clustering settings match the settings stated for the reported result, and an observable code output or assertion reconciles those settings with the reported memberships, counts, and summaries; or no clustering claim is made.", "label": "A", "points": 0}, {"description": "A clustering result is reported with mostly matching executable settings, but reconciliation is incomplete or a limited discrepancy affects some reported memberships or summaries without invalidating the main scoped result.", "label": "B", "points": -5}, {"description": "The executable primary clustering uses materially different settings from those named in the results, so reported memberships, counts, or summaries do not come from the claimed analysis and are not repaired or clearly qualified.", "label": "C", "points": -10}]

title: Executable clustering and reported-results consistency

levels: [{"description": "No clinical/prospective predictive claim is made, or any such claim is accurately qualified as hypothesis-generating association evidence with the need for independent prospective validation and predictive-performance assessment; the method and scope match the claim.", "label": "A", "points": 0}, {"description": "A predictive-biomarker or clinical-use implication is present but is materially softened or scoped incompletely—for example, it acknowledges association or noncausality but omits either prospective validation or predictive-performance assessment.", "label": "B", "points": -5}, {"description": "The artifact presents postmortem cross-sectional associations as usable clinical or prospective predictive biomarkers without the required validation and performance evidence, materially overstating what the analysis supports.", "label": "C", "points": -10}]

Retain the underlying association analysis and qualified interpretation.
title: Predictive-biomarker claim is supported and scoped

levels: [{"description": "The artifact makes no covered independent-validation claim, or reports validation using a preregistered/pre-specified or genuinely independent sample rule unrelated to candidate values, with the method, scope, and limitation accurately stated.", "label": "A", "points": 0}, {"description": "A candidate-defined exclusion or other dependence affects a validation/robustness analysis, but it is clearly labeled exploratory, the untrimmed or otherwise valid result is retained, and no independent-confirmation claim is made.", "label": "B", "points": -5}, {"description": "The artifact presents a candidate-defined, post-selection exclusion as independent validation, or bases the covered validation claim on it without disclosing the dependence or retaining the valid full-sample result.", "label": "C", "points": -10}]
requirement: For any candidate selected from the same data, check that the reported validation or robustness statistic uses a sample-inclusion rule fixed before candidate selection and independent of candidate values; if candidate-defined trimming is used, label it exploratory sensitivity analysis and do not present it as independent validation. Retain the full eligible-case result and accurately state the scope and limitation.
title: Independence of Candidate Validation

levels: [{"description": "No covered independent-validation claim is made, or the artifact demonstrates that validation participants/donors are disjoint from discovery and accurately states the validation scope and limitation.", "label": "A", "points": 0}, {"description": "The artifact uses ambiguous or insufficient support for an independent-validation implication, such as relying on a separate tissue file without a clear donor-overlap check, but labels the result as replication/reproducibility or otherwise avoids a definite false claim.", "label": "B", "points": -5}, {"description": "The artifact explicitly presents another tissue or dataset as independent validation solely because it is separately filed or measured, without demonstrating participant/donor disjointness, and fails to disclose that independent validation remains unestablished.", "label": "C", "points": -10}]
requirement: When an artifact calls a result from another tissue or dataset “independent validation,” check the documented sample or donor identifiers for disjointness from discovery; a separate file or tissue level alone is insufficient. If disjointness is unverified, report cross-tissue reproducibility/replication instead, retain valid full-case results, and state that independent participant-level validation remains pending.
title: Participant Independence for Independent Validation

levels: [{"description": "No covered predictive claim is made, or any such claim is supported by documented prospective longitudinal validation or an independently evaluated prediction model. The artifact accurately states the observational scope and limitation while retaining the reported association.", "label": "A", "points": 0}, {"description": "The artifact uses ambiguous or mildly overstated predictive language about the cross-sectional association, but also qualifies it as needing prospective validation and does not clearly claim established clinical prediction or identification of fast progressors.", "label": "B", "points": -5}, {"description": "The artifact presents the postmortem duration association as established predictive utility, a predictive biomarker, or evidence that expression can identify fast progressors without prospective longitudinal validation or an independently evaluated prediction model, despite the evidence being observational and cross-sectional.", "label": "C", "points": -10}]
requirement: When reporting a postmortem, cross-sectional association between gene expression and recorded disease duration, check that the artifact labels it observational or candidate-biomarker evidence rather than established prediction, predictive utility, or identification of fast progressors, unless prospective longitudinal validation or an independently evaluated prediction model is documented; retain the association, method, scope, and limitation.
title: Scope of Postmortem Duration Associations

levels: [{"description": "The artifact either makes no covered confirmatory/mechanistic claim or transparently reports the parallel-test scope and uses suitable multiplicity control, or accurately labels unadjusted findings exploratory with appropriately limited interpretation.", "label": "A", "points": 0}, {"description": "The artifact avoids claiming confirmed mechanistic separation but incompletely reports the number or scope of parallel tests, the adjustment plan, or the exploratory qualification, leaving the evidential status materially ambiguous.", "label": "B", "points": -5}, {"description": "The artifact uses nominal unadjusted significance from multiple residue-level tests as confirmed evidence of distinct mechanisms or mechanistic separation, without appropriate multiplicity control or an accurate exploratory qualification.", "label": "C", "points": -10}]
requirement: When multiple residue-level significance tests are used to support a confirmatory or mechanistic conclusion, report the tested multiplicity, apply an appropriate multiplicity adjustment, or explicitly label the findings exploratory, and do not treat nominal unadjusted significance as confirmed mechanistic separation. Preserve the underlying composition results and any qualified interpretation.
title: Multiplicity control for parallel residue tests

levels: [{"description": "The trace makes sheet selection and workbook resolution, header treatment, dimensions/counts, and duplicate or multi-gene handling independently verifiable; the supplied code implements the stated operations and supports reproducible joining, or no covered claim is made.", "label": "A", "points": 0}, {"description": "The trace documents most relevant loading and duplicate-resolution decisions but leaves one material detail ambiguous, such as incomplete count checkpoints, weak sheet/header verification, or an incompletely specified aggregation rule, limiting independent reproduction without wholly defeating the integrated result.", "label": "B", "points": -5}, {"description": "Sheet selection or header treatment is hard-coded or unverifiable, key dimensions/counts are not reproducible, or duplicate/multi-gene records are described without a concrete implemented resolution rule, materially undermining verification of the integrated gene set.", "label": "C", "points": -10}]
requirement: When multiple workbook sheets, header rows, or duplicate protein records can affect the integrated gene set, provide an auditable trace that names the selected sheets, resolves them through workbook metadata, identifies removed title/header rows, reports dimensions or counts before and after each operation, and explicitly states and implements the duplicate/multi-gene aggregation rule before joining. Counts must be reproducible from the supplied code.
